questions.question: What does the Electoral College process select?
choices: Members of the Supreme Court
President and vice president
State governors
Members of the House

questions.question: How is a state's number of presidential electors determined?
choices: Its land area divided by counties
Its number of state legislators
Its number of registered political parties
Its total House and Senate representation

questions.question: What is the minimum number of electors for a state?
choices: Three
One
Two
Five

questions.question: Which amendment provided presidential electors for the District of Columbia?
choices: Twelfth Amendment
Seventeenth Amendment
Twenty-third Amendment
Twenty-second Amendment

questions.question: Which amendment requires distinct electoral votes for president and vice president?
choices: First Amendment
Twelfth Amendment
Fourteenth Amendment
Twenty-sixth Amendment

questions.question: What electoral-vote threshold normally elects a president?
choices: A majority of appointed electors
The largest total even without a majority
One-third of all electors
A unanimous vote of all electors

questions.question: Which chamber chooses the president if no candidate receives the required electoral majority?
choices: Senate
Supreme Court
State governors collectively
House of Representatives

questions.question: How do most states award electoral votes under their established practice?
choices: In exact proportion to each candidate's national vote
By the governor's personal choice after election day
Through a winner-take-all system based on the state's popular vote
Through a vote of the Supreme Court

questions.question: Why can a national popular-vote winner lose the presidency?
choices: Electoral votes are awarded through state-based rules rather than one national tally
The national popular vote automatically overrides electors
Each state receives the same number of electors
Votes in presidential elections are counted only in the capital

questions.question: What distinguishes Maine and Nebraska's allocation method from most states?
choices: They receive no presidential electors
They award some electors by congressional district results
They use only a nationwide popular-vote total
They choose the president through their governors

questions.question: How does the House vote in a contingent presidential election?
choices: Each representative casts one electoral vote based on district population
Each governor casts two votes
Each state receives votes equal to its electoral allocation
Each state delegation casts one vote

questions.question: Who chooses the vice president if no candidate receives the required electoral majority?
choices: House of Representatives
Supreme Court
Senate
National governors' association

questions.question: Why can closely divided states receive heavy campaign attention?
choices: Changing their outcome may change which candidate receives their electors
Campaigns are legally forbidden in all other states
Their voters cast ballots worth more than any state's electoral total
Their governors directly elect the president

questions.question: What do voters generally select when voting for a presidential ticket?
choices: Supreme Court nominees listed on the same ballot
A slate of electors pledged to that ticket
A national cabinet chosen independently of candidates
The next speaker of the House

questions.question: Why are electors not the same as members of Congress?
choices: They write all federal election laws
They approve all judicial appointments
They serve as permanent members of the Senate
They perform a separate constitutional role in presidential selection

questions.question: A state has eight representatives and two senators. How many presidential electors does it have?
choices: Eight
Two
Ten
Sixteen

questions.question: A candidate wins a winner-take-all state's popular vote by a narrow margin. What generally follows?
choices: The candidate's slate receives that state's electoral votes
The state's electors are divided exactly by vote percentage
The governor receives the state's votes
The state loses its electoral representation

questions.question: No presidential candidate receives an electoral majority. Which constitutional process applies?
choices: A new national referendum required by the Constitution
A contingent election in the House
Automatic selection of the popular-vote runner-up
Selection by the Chief Justice alone

questions.question: Which comparison of popular and electoral votes is accurate?
choices: Both are identical totals expressed in different units
Electoral votes count only ballots cast by senators
Popular votes are cast only after electors have voted
Popular votes count individual ballots; electoral votes reflect the state-based constitutional process

questions.question: Why should a student examine state allocation rules when analyzing an election?
choices: Every state must divide electors proportionally
Allocation rules determine who serves as Chief Justice
States may award electors differently, affecting the path to an electoral majority
State rules replace the constitutional majority requirement
